title: MS GTM BUILDERS AND PROMOTERS PVT LTD versus MS FUN GATEWAY ARENA PVT LTD

paras.text:
UKHC010171052025
2026:UHC:8196
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE SHRI MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA
11TH SEPTEMBER, 2026
ARBITRATION APPLICATION No. 56 OF 2025
1: MS GTM Builders And Promoters Pvt. Ltd.
--Petitioner
Versus
2: MS Fun Gateway Arena Pvt. Ltd.
--Respondent Counsel for the applicant.

: Mr. Gaurav Sindhwani, learned counsel
with Mr. Rishab Ranghar, learned
counsel.
JUDGMENT :
1. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. On 14.08.2026, the following order was passed by
this Court :-
"1. The present application has been filed under Section
11(6) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 for
appointment of an Arbitrator for deciding the dispute in
respect of arrears of license fees under the License Agreement
between the parties dated 30th October, 2023. The said
agreement was followed by an addendum dated 15th May,
2024.
2. Clause 13f of the agreement provides for resolution of
disputes between the parties arising out of the agreement by a
sole Arbitrator, who shall be a retired High Court Judge, jointly
nominated by the parties. The seat of Arbitration would be at
Dehradun. Clause 13f is extracted below:-
"f. In the event of any dispute, controversy, claim or conflict
between the Parties arising out of or relating to this Agreement
(including issues relating to the performance or non-performance of
the obligations set out herein or the breach, termination or invalidity
thereof) (a "Dispute"), such Dispute shall be referred to a sole
arbitrator, who shall be a retired high court judge who is jointly
nominated by the Parties. The arbitration proceedings shall be
convened under the provisions of the Arbitration and Conciliation
Act, 1996 and the award so granted by the sole arbitrator shall be
final and binding on the Parties. The language of the arbitration
shall be English, and the seat of the arbitration shall be Dehradun."
3. The applicant had invoked the arbitration clause by a
notice dated 11.09.2025. The notice was sent to the opposite
party by registered post and the postal receipts evidencing the
said fact have been filed at Page No.61 of the application. The

track consignment report of India Post has also been filed to
prove service of notice on the opposite party.
4. However, according to the applicant, no reply has been
submitted thereto by the opposite party. In the application
invoking arbitration clause, the applicant has proposed name
of three retired Judges of Delhi High Court, but as noted
above, the notice has not been replied to by the opposite party
and thus, in absence of consensus to the name of the
Arbitrator, the applicant has been compelled to approach this
Court for appointment of an Arbitrator.
5. It is noteworthy that in response to an earlier notice of
the applicant dated 08.08.2025, the opposite party had given
a reply and in Paragraph No.3 thereof, although liability to pay
the arrears of license fees is admitted, the quantum has been
disputed.
6. The opposite party has been duly served by registered
post and on the previous date also, nobody appeared on
behalf of the opposite party, but in the interest of justice, the
matter was adjourned awaiting appearance. Today also, there
is no representation on behalf of the opposite party.
7. Learned counsel for the applicant very fairly states that
this Court may nominate any independent arbitrator, who may
be a retired High Court Judge, and he has no objection to the
same.
8. Having regard to the Arbitration agreement and the fact
that the parties have failed to arrive at consensus on the name
of the arbitrator, this Court is of the opinion that an
independent arbitrator should be appointed to resolve the
disputes between the parties.
9. The Court, accordingly, proposes the name of Mr. Justice
Mehboob Ali, retired Judge Allahabad High Court (Mobile
No.9473687398), R/o 90 Majra West, Near Masjid Majra,
Dehradun as the sole Arbitrator to resolve the disputes
between the parties arising out of the License Agreement. The
seat of arbitration shall be at Dehradun.
10. Let necessary disclosures and consent in terms of
Section 11(8) of the Act be obtained from the Arbitrator within
two weeks and thereafter the matter be listed for further
orders before the Court"
3. As per the office report dated 09.09.2026, the
necessary disclosures and consent has been received from the
proposed Arbitrator - Mr. Justice Mehboob Ali, retired Judge
Allahabad High Court for being appointed as Arbitrator to
resolve the dispute(s) between the parties.

4. Accordingly, Mr. Justice Mehboob Ali, retired Judge
Allahabad High Court is appointed as Arbitrator to resolve the
dispute(s) between the parties.
5. The office is directed to inform the Arbitrator to
proceed.
6. The Arbitration Application stands disposed of
accordingly.
7. Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of
accordingly.

______________________
MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA, C.J.
Dt: 11th September, 2026
Rahul
